verdict.rationale: First-party docs say that with App Lock enabled, Authenticator requires the device PIN or a biometric every time it is opened. The docs also state that App Lock protects the one-time codes, app information and settings, so a borrowed phone does not expose codes. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration of App Lock behavior, and documentation of whether it is on by default and how it handles re-locking on resume.

support.subject: As an everyday user, the app itself locks behind biometrics or a PIN, so a borrowed phone doesn't expose my codes

citations.quote: When App Lock is enabled, you'll be asked to authenticate using your device PIN or biometric every time you open Authenticator.
App Lock helps keep your one-time verification codes, app information, and app settings more secure.
